newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE RESPONDING WELL TO TREATMENT.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-CRIVILLE RESPONDING WELL TO TREATMENT.

text.p: Spain's Alex Criville is responding well to treatment to hand injuries sustained in last week Dutch Grand Prix but may need another skin graft on his thumb, his Repsol Honda team said on Friday.

Criville suffered tendon and bone damage to his left hand and wrist when he lost control of his bike on a chicane at Assen last Thursday. The bike slid over the tarmac with his arm trapped underneath.
He is in hospital in Barcelona where he had surgery on Wednesday to see if initial skin grafts carried out in the Netherlands were successful.

"Doctors at the clinic reported that the nerves and tendons...were responding well and that they were certain full mobility of the wrist would be restored," Repsol Honda said in a statement issued during Friday's practice session for the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola.
"However, the lack of movement in his thumb is causing a little concern and it will also require a further skin-graft. A decision will be made tomorrow concerning further treatment."
Criville has already been ruled out of the 500cc world championship until at least September but Repsol said they had no plans to replace him.
